AgriFresh Foods Corp. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AgriFresh Foods Corp. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AgriFresh Foods Corp.'s Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Roberto Garcia, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, organic revenue growth overall and by region, our reaffirmed full-year guidance, e-commerce sales growth and its contribution to total revenue, the impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, the impact of new product innovations and launches, and our EPS guidance and key assumptions.

First, on the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, we've navigated significant pressures in our packaged foods and beverages segment, including brands like FreshHarvest snacks, PureSpring bottled waters, and AgriBrew ready-to-drink teas, but our strategies preserved profitability. COGS rose 12.8% year-over-year against 7.2% revenue growth, driven by agricultural input spikes—wheat flour up 22% from Russia-Ukraine effects and U.S. droughts, corn derivatives up 16%, edible oils like soybean and palm up 25% due to Indonesian restrictions and European biofuel demand, sugar up 14% from Brazilian harvest issues, poultry up 20% from avian flu, and dairy up 11% from New Zealand weather. Logistics costs jumped 14%, with ocean freight from Asia up 35% on Red Sea issues and port congestion, North American trucking up 12%, and rail delays adding weeks to grain shipments, hitting inventory by 4.5% and requiring premium air freight for 8% of SKUs. Regionally, North America saw 15% inflation, Europe 22% from energy crises, APAC 28% on palm oil, and LatAm 30% effective from Argentine currency woes. This compressed gross margins 210 bps to 32.4% and EBITDA margins to 14.1%, but pricing offset much of it.

Second, our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies drove key growth, with RGM levers—pricing at 5.5 points, mix management growth at 1.2 points, and volume at 0.5 points—fueling 7.2% organic revenue growth. We took targeted 4.8% average increases on 75% of portfolio, calibrated by elasticity: 3-5% in staples like Fresha Cola passing 60% of 8.2% input inflation, 6-8% in premium indulgence like NutriCrunch bars and SurgeMax drinks with 0.65 elasticity. Net realization hit 5.5%, trade spend steady at 14.2%. Mix shifted to better-for-you SKUs, plant-based at 22% of beverages up from 15%, OatFlex milk grabbing share. Volumes resilient, indulgence up 2.1%. Regionally, North America 8.5% ORG, Europe 5.1%, APAC/LatAm 7.8%.

Third, organic revenue growth was solid at 7.1% overall, year-to-date 6.8%, eighth straight positive quarter outpacing industry 4%. Pricing 4.2 points, volume/mix 2.9 points from e-com velocity and share gains. North America 8.3% on RTD beverages like Apex Hydrate, Europe 5.4% on plant-based snacks, APAC 9.6% on RTD teas in China/India, LatAm 6.7% despite FX.

Fourth, we're reaffirming full-year guidance with an upward EPS revision. Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 32.4%, impacted by input cost inflation and supply chain pressures as Mike outlined. Operating income was $403 million, and earnings per share were $1.05. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic growth of 6-7%, adjusted gross margins expanding 140-160 bps to 38.5-39%, EBITDA $2.45-$2.55 billion, free cash flow $1.6-$1.8 billion, and narrowing adjusted diluted EPS to $4.65-$4.85, up from prior $4.50-$4.75.

To expand on the key areas Mike highlighted, let's drill deeper starting with input costs and supply chain. These headwinds were prominent, but our playbook mitigated them effectively. We've hedged 70% of 2024 grain via CBOT futures at 10-15% below spot, fixed 85% of palm oil versus 60% last year. Supply chain resilience includes reducing China packaging reliance from 40% to 25% via Mexico/India, SAP S&OP with Blue Yonder AI boosting forecast accuracy to 92%, cutting safety stock 18% and avoiding $25M write-downs, plus verticalizing 12% corn processing in a U.S. JV. Product shifts reformulated 40% snacks with stevia-maltitol cutting sugar 15%, organic granolas up 15% volume, RSPO palm at 95%. Q4 inflation eases to 6-8%, freight down 10-15%, though El Niño cocoa risks linger; guidance embeds $150-200M COGS inflation offset by 7-9% pricing for 33.5% margins and 8% EBITDA growth. Peers saw 300 bps compression per IRI; ours was 150 bps better.

On pricing and RGM, this framework maximized top-line via pricing, MMG, and volume. Pricing power from #2 salty snacks share behind Frito-Lay at 18% per Circana. Zero-based pricing with NielsenIQ/IRI AI on 150K POS scans weekly. Dynamic pilots in 1,200 Albertsons doors adjust via ML on competitors/weather. Revenue Optimization Center with SAP IBP/ML simulates 10K scenarios at 92% elasticity accuracy. Blockchain for cocoa/palm hedges 15% 2024 inputs. Q4 pricing 4-5%, ORG 6-8%. $250M innovation pipeline for mix gains, targeting 200 bps gross uplift by FY25.

Organic growth details show balance: pricing 4.2 points on functionals/premiums like Zero Sugar Energy/Protein Bites, volume/mix from pruning low-velocity for 120 bps mix gain. North America 45% revenue, 8.3% ORG on RTDs gaining 1.2 points sports hydration share, snacks +6% Walmart/Kroger/Amazon wins, premium up 12%. Europe 5.4%, volumes flat+ via VitaCrunch pea protein 25% growth UK/Germany, €50M sustainable certs. APAC 9.6%, China bubble teas $10B market 8% CAGR Tmall/JD.com, India hydration +14% rural nets. LatAm 6.7%, premium beer adjacencies +18% Mexico. R&D 2.8% sales, 15 SKUs functionals like collagen yogurts/keto chips, Apex Rewards app 10M users +22% repeats, 65% regenerative ag -12% Scope 3.

Full-year guidance reaffirmed with EPS lift reflects Q3 strength, margin initiatives, demand resilience in beverages/snacks/plant-based. Sales $12.4-12.7B, 5-7% organic. EPS $3.95-4.10 prior now $4.65-4.85, $150M gross expansion from AI forecasting 15% inventory cuts, cocoa stabilizing $10K/MT, dairy 2-3%. Productivity via Harvest Efficiency 2.0 precision ag Brazil/Midwest 8% yields stevia/almonds. OpEx 3-4% growth zero-based, SAP S/4HANA 80% live -10% indirect spend. FCF 13-14% sales, CapEx 4.5% aseptic Mexico. North America low-mid single digits ZeroWave +25%, EMEA flat-2% PureSpring +18%, APAC/LatAm double-digits China e-com GreenLeaf. Pillars: premiumization 12 SKUs stevia RTD coffee 30% repeats, Scope 3 -12% regen cocoa EU compliant. Risks ocean freight +5%, El Niño coffee; $100M contingency, 70% FX hedge.

E-commerce surged to $285M, +42% YoY, 22.3% total revenue up from 16.8%, 11th triple-digit quarter. Snacks 28%, beverages 25%, meals 18% subscription 12% DTC. North America $194M +45% nutrifresh.com 2.5M MAUs Amazon/Instacart 55% GMV AOV $48 bundling. EMEA $52M +35% Shopify Ocado 15 dark stores <2hr delivery +22% conversion. APAC $39M +62% Tmall/Flipkart millet snacks AOV $35 WeChat. Adobe/AWS omnichannel -40% stockouts BOPIS 25%, Vertex AI +28% repeats. NutriFresh Club 450K members $68M recurring <4% churn LTV $450 CAC $22 TikTok/Instagram. 100% recyclable liners -30% emissions blockchain organics +15% AOV. E-com margins 42% vs 38%, fulfillment 11%. To 28-30% FY25 $450-500M, Walmart+ LATAM Mercado Libre Alexa.

FX was a 4.5 point $128M headwind, constant currency +7.2%, YTD $285M 3.8 points drag. 58% international: Europe euro -8.2% $62M + pound -5.4% $18M, PureSpring/AquaFizz +9.1% const but 1% reported. LatAm BRL -12.1% MXN -7.3% $45M +11% const flat reported. APAC AUD/JPY -6.8/-9.5% $22M ZenLeaf +8% const -2% reported. USD index +11%. Q4 $90-110M more. Hedged 72% collars/forwards/natural, protected $45M EBITDA vs Pepsi 65%. Pricing 5-7% recovers 60-70% elasticity -1.2, localize PET Brazil -15% USD inputs, Poland blending PLN stable, AI SAP/Bloomberg dynamic 14 currencies. Glocal: India +22% sachets, premium RTD coffee +15%.

New innovations drove 28% top-line, NPI $1.2B T12M +42%, 76% success >65% industry, 14K ACV points 22-31% penetration. VitaGlow RTD adaptogens/protein $320M +180% 48.2% margins $3.49/can Mexico/Poland co-man -15% COGS. PlantPower bars $210M +95% pea JV 68% repeats upcycled 62% consumer priority +22% velocity Whole Foods. NA 58% NPI 15.2% 4.2 share RTD DSD 85K -5% OOS +320 bps margins. APAC 22% VitaFerment yuzu/matcha $150M +140% 18% CAGR Shopee >35% trial Indonesia inflation -150 bps pouch -12%. EMEA 9% VitaBloom baby pouches $95M +75% 2.8 share HFSS tax exemptions Tesco +28%. Health Horizon: precision ferm Ginkgo alt-milk -30% whey, 12 FY24 launches electrolyte/ spent grain $2.5B proj 50%+ margins 3x ROI 18mo. 65% EPS beat.

EPS guidance $4.65-4.85 8-11% midpoint Q4 $1.35-1.45. Organic 5-7% Q4 6-8% pricing 4-5% cocoa +25% oils disciplined premium zero-sugar +15%, volume/mix +1-2% plant-based +12% club Costco. Gross +150-250 bps 42.5% dairy defl -5-7% hedge 70% cocoa, $250-300M productivity AI FourKites -8% logistics precision Brazil sugar -10% waste, close 2 facilities megaplants Mexico/Poland. SG&A 22-23% -50 bps zero-based CTV/TikTok 40% Gen Z PlantVita e-com +25%. Tax 23-24% interest $120M 4.2% bonds no M&A dil. NA 6-8% low/no sugar 35% +2 share holiday +50 bps, EMEA 3-5% value promos euro FX -1, APAC/LatAm 8-10% China dbl dig Brazil +15% India monsoon risk. Power brands 90% 2025 $400M dairy divest $1B buyback $45-50/share net-zero 2040 regen cocoa Barry 15% risk mit. Upside comm relief/M&A downside infl/palm +10% recession; 45% EBITDA resilient.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, John. As we detailed, input inflation hit hard with 12.8% COGS rise, ag inputs up sharply across wheat, corn, oils, sugar, proteins, dairy. Supply disruptions added freight spikes and inventory hits, compressing margins 210 bps. But hedging 70-85% key commodities, diversification from China, AI S&OP 92% accuracy, reformulations, and 8-10% pricing rounds limited damage to 150 bps versus peers' 300 bps. Q4 moderates to 6-8%, guidance buffers it fully.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product and what is the expected impact of product?

David Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Innovations are core, with 2.8% sales to R&D yielding 28% top-line contribution, NPI $1.2B +42%, 76% success. VitaGlow functionals $320M +180% 550 bps margin lift, PlantPower bars $210M +95% upcycled sustainability edge. Regional ramps: NA 15.2% share gains, APAC 22% fermented +140%, EMEA baby pouches +75% tax-smart. Pipeline 12 launches $2.5B high-margin, driving 4-6% long-term ORG acceleration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Roberto Garcia (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Mike. Disruptions inflated logistics 14%, ocean +35%, trucking +12%, rail delays. We countered with sourcing diversification—packaging China to 25%, corn JV vertical 12%, SAP/Blue Yonder AI 92% forecasts -18% stock, avoiding $25M excess. Regional stability: NA domestic corn/soy, Europe energy hedge, APAC palm fixed, LatAm blockchain coffee/cocoa -5% costs. Panama easing aids Q4.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Laura, Q4 ORG 6-8%, EPS $1.35-1.45, full-year organic 5-7% midpoint high-end holiday/emerging momentum. Gross expansion 150-250 bps productivity $250-300M AI routing/precision ag/facility shifts, pricing 4-5% offsets cocoa/oils. NA premium/holiday tailwinds, EMEA cautious volume, APAC/LatAm engine. FX/commodity risks hedged 70-80%, contingency in place for resilient upper-half delivery.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in AgriFresh Foods Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
